newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-JADEJA HELPS INDIA POST 220 IN LATE SURGE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JADEJA HELPS INDIA POST 220 IN LATE SURGE.

text.p: A late flourish in the closing overs from Ajay Jadeja enabled India to post a respectable total of 220 for seven from their 50 overs against South Africa in the final of the Titan Cup triangular one-day series on Wednesday.

Despite the loss of two early wickets, India appeared to be cruising comfortably as skipper Sachin Tendulkar, who had won the toss and elected to bat first, and the in-form Mohammad Azharuddin added 48 in even time for the third wicket.
But when Azharuddin, who made 26, and Tendulkar, who top-scored with 67 from 89 balls, both fell to the left-arm spin of Nicky Boje, the innings began to flounder.

India's efforts to break the stranglehold imposed by some accurate South African bowling and some superb ground fielding only resulted in the hosts losing several quick wickets and they crumbled to 153 for six.
In the closing overs, however, the Indians struck back with their best partnership of the innings as Jadeja and Nayan Mongia put on 51 from 53 balls.
Jadeja was at his breezy best with an unbeaten 43 from 42 deliveries which included two sixes off successive balls from Boje as well as two boundaries.
Fanie de Villiers, who opened the South African attack, again bowled economically, conceding only four runs in his first four overs and ending with three for 32.
